speaker: Unknown
en: 20 months ago, we didn't have a robot.
zh: 20个月前，我们没有机器人。

speaker: Unknown
en: We had smiles on our faces and the idea of humanoid, right?
zh: 我们脸上带着微笑，有着人形机器人的想法，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And today we have robots already deployed out in the world, working full shifts.
zh: 而今天我们已经部署了机器人在世界上，工作整整轮班。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think all of this is a lot closer than anyone will think.
zh: 我认为这一切比任何人想的都要近得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: I wrote something last year about humanoids and how the promise is way out ahead of the reality.
zh: 我去年写了一些关于人形机器人的东西，以及承诺是如何远远领先于现实的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there are all these problems with power supply and the strength of
zh: 并且存在所有这些关于电源供应和强度的问题

speaker: Unknown
en: We're also trying to get the robots out, that's why I say onto the battlefield in Ukraine, to really hope to actually start putting them out there and seeing how do the soldiers want to use them?
zh: 我们也在试图把机器人弄出去，这就是为什么我说到乌克兰的战场，真的希望实际上开始把它们放在那里，看看士兵们想怎么使用它们？

speaker: Unknown
en: How do they actually work in a fight?
zh: 它们在战斗中实际上是如何工作的？

speaker: Unknown
en: How do they go up against drones?
zh: 它们如何对抗无人机？

speaker: Unknown
en: How do they go up against explosions?
zh: 它们如何对抗爆炸？

speaker: Unknown
en: Co-founder of Foundation Robotics Lab back in January when the company was making a public relations push claiming they were building humanoid robot soldiers.
zh: Foundation Robotics Lab 的联合创始人，早在一月当公司正在进行公关推动时声称他们正在建造人形机器人士兵。

speaker: Unknown
en: Mike was claiming they would produce 10,000 robots this year when even Tesla fell far short of the 5,000 it had hoped to make in 2025.
zh: Mike 声称他们今年将生产 10,000 台机器人，而甚至特斯拉也远未达到其 2025 年希望制造的 5,000 台。

speaker: Unknown
en: Mike is good company, smart, engaging, and by his own description, an optimist to the core.
zh: Mike 很好的公司，聪明，迷人，而且他自己的描述，一个核心的乐观主义者。

speaker: Unknown
en: I, on the other hand, am a skeptic to the core.
zh: 我，另一方面，是一个核心的怀疑论者。

speaker: Unknown
en: At the end of our podcast recording, I asked if I could tag along to Ukraine when he delivered robots there for testing.
zh: 在我们的播客录音结束时，我问是否可以当他交付机器人去那里测试时一起去乌克兰。

speaker: Unknown
en: The trip happened in February.
zh: 这趟旅行发生在二月。

speaker: Unknown
en: We got to Kiev, but the robots were stopped at the Polish border and never arrived.
zh: 我们到了基辅，但机器人被阻止在波兰边境并且从未到达。

speaker: Unknown
en: Nonetheless, Mike's public relations team managed to get a big spread in Time, the venerable media brand now owned by Marc Benioff, Salesforce's CEO.
zh: 尽管如此，Mike 的公关团队设法在《时代》周刊上获得了大幅报道，这个受人尊敬的媒体品牌现在由 Salesforce 的 CEO Marc Benioff 拥有。

speaker: Unknown
en: The article talks a lot about robotic warfare, but fudges the question of whether any foundation robots ever made it to Ukraine.
zh: 这篇文章谈了很多关于机器人战争的内容，但回避了任何 Foundation 机器人是否真的到达了乌克兰的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: It said simply that in February, two Phantoms were sent to Ukraine, initially for frontline reconnaissance support.
zh: 它简单地说在二月，两个 Phantom 被送往乌克兰，最初用于前线侦察支持。

speaker: Unknown
en: But that was enough for news aggregators to pick it up, and pretty soon I was seeing headlines like, robots in real war, Ukraine battlefield tests Phantom Mach 1, Ukraine deploys humanoid robots in battlefield reconnaissance, and robots are heading to war, being tested in Ukraine.
zh: 但这足以让新闻聚合媒体抓取它，很快我就看到像这样的标题，机器人真正的战争，乌克兰战场测试 Phantom Mach 1，乌克兰部署人形机器人进行战场侦察，以及机器人正在走向战争，在乌克兰进行测试。

speaker: Unknown
en: When I visited Foundations Operations in San Francisco in April, my skepticism grew.
zh: 当我在四月访问 Foundation 在旧金山的业务时，我的怀疑态度增长了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Mike's claim that the company went from an idea to building a complete humanoid in under two years left out that he and his founders started by buying an existing humanoid robot company named Boardwalk.
zh: Mike 声称公司在不到两年的时间里从一个想法变成了建造一个完整的人形机器人，这漏掉了他和他的创始人们是通过购买一家名为 Boardwalk 的现成人形机器人公司开始的。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's more, some of the military contracts he mentions were carried over from that earlier company.
zh: 而且，他提到的一些军事合同是从那家早期的公司继承过来的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Foundation Shop felt like a research lab, not a factory.
zh: Foundation 的车间感觉像一个研究实验室，而不是工厂。

speaker: Unknown
en: The robots on the floor were relatively lightweight machines, nothing that could withstand the recoil of a military weapon.
zh: 地板上的机器人是相对轻型的机器，没有任何东西能承受军事武器的后坐力。

speaker: Unknown
en: An engineer giving me the tour gave one a shove and it stumbled onto its knees held up by a harness.
zh: 一位带我参观的工程师推了一个，它跌跌撞撞地跪在地上，被安全带支撑着。

speaker: Unknown
en: The operation was producing about one robot a day, which made 10,000 this year seem impossible.
zh: 该作业每天生产大约一台机器人，这使得今年的 10,000 台看起来不可能。

speaker: Unknown
en: The whole time I kept trying to square what I saw with the company's pitch.
zh: 整个时间我一直试图把我看到的和公司的推销结合起来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Machines that would cross rough terrain in a war zone and carry weapons.
zh: 那些将在战区穿越崎岖地形并携带武器的机器。

speaker: Unknown
en: I spoke to Mike recently and he has several updates.
zh: 我最近和 Mike 谈过，他有几个更新。

speaker: Unknown
en: A new more robust model of the robot has been completed.
zh: 一个新的更强大的机器人模型已经完成了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Six feet tall, 185 pounds with arms that Mike claims can each lift 80 kilos, more than 170 pounds each.
zh: 六英尺高，185磅，手臂 Mike 声称每一个可以提升 80 公斤，每一个超过 170 磅。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the company is opening a new production facility in Texas.
zh: 而且公司正在德克萨斯开设一个新的生产设施。

speaker: Unknown
en: They've scaled back this year's production target to 6,000 robots instead of 10,000.
zh: 他们已将今年的生产目标缩减到 6,000 台机器人，而不是 10,000 台。

speaker: Unknown
en: Mike said that Foundation is building its own AI model to control the robot.
zh: Mike 说 Foundation 正在建立自己的 AI 模型来控制机器人。

speaker: Unknown
en: But see my earlier episode with Sergey Levine, a renowned AI researcher with his own startup, Physical Intelligence, where he talks about how difficult that is to do.
zh: 但请看我之前与 Sergey Levine 的一集，他是一位著名的 AI 研究员，拥有自己的初创公司 Physical Intelligence，他在谈话中谈到这有多困难。

speaker: Unknown
en: Mike said Foundation is building its own actuators.
zh: Mike 说 Foundation 正在建立自己的执行器。

speaker: Unknown
en: The tiny motors that control the robot's joints and are the most critical part in any humanoid.
zh: 那些控制机器人关节的微型电机，是任何机器人中最关键的部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's ambitious.
zh: 那是雄心勃勃的。

speaker: Unknown
en: None of this means Foundation won't get there.
zh: 这并不意味着 Foundation 不会到达那里。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've been confidently skeptical about companies before and turned out to be wrong.
zh: 我以前曾对公司自信地怀疑过，结果证明我错了。

speaker: Unknown
en: As I told Mike, Foundation's PR is running far faster than its robots.
zh: 正如我告诉 Mike 的，Foundation 的公关远比它的机器人跑得快。

speaker: Unknown
en: Here's the conversation.
zh: 这是对话。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why don't we start with having you introduce yourself and talk about your earlier startup, and then we'll get into Foundation and what you guys are doing.
zh: 我们何不从让你自我介绍并谈谈你之前的初创公司开始，然后我们会进入 Foundation 以及你们正在做的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Great.
zh: 太好了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, so I'm Michael LeBlanc.
zh: 是的，我是 Michael LeBlanc。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was born and raised in Ohio and then left home to go to Annapolis, Maryland, where I studied the classics and solved the books behind me, learned to translate ancient Greek out there, and got deep into the classics.
zh: 我在俄亥俄州出生长大，然后离开家去了马里兰州的安纳波利斯，在那里我学习古典文学并解决了我身后的书，学会了在那里翻译古希腊文，并深入钻研了古典文学。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as I did, that started to make me really look at war in a deep way, you know, looking at Thucydides and Plutarch and Aramides.
zh: 当我这样做时，这开始让我真正以深刻的方式看待战争，你知道，看着修昔底德、普鲁塔克和阿米尼亚德斯。

speaker: Unknown
en: And joined the Marine Corps, much to my family's dismay.
zh: 并加入了海军陆战队，这让我家人的大为惊恐。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was in the Marine Corps for 12 years total.
zh: 我在海军陆战队总共待了 12 年。

speaker: Unknown
en: I did three tours to the Middle East during that time.
zh: 在此期间，我三次前往中东执行任务。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was at the Pentagon.
zh: 我曾在五角大楼任职。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it was at the Pentagon that I started looking at startups.
zh: 正是在五角大楼，我开始关注初创公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was looking at electric tanks and starting to vet what, you know, pocket drones, how these things could actually come in, how they could be used.
zh: 当时我在研究电动坦克，并开始审查，你知道，袖珍无人机，这些东西实际上如何进入，如何被使用。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so as I did that, it started to make me really look at a lot of these companies.
zh: 正因如此，我开始真正审视许多这些公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was getting married at the same time.
zh: 同时我也在准备结婚。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so got out of the Marine Corps, went to Harvard Business School, and then as I was out of there, co-founded Cobalt Robotics, which was back to, you know, we did our seed through Bloomberg Beta, our A through Sequoia, our B through CO2.
zh: 所以我离开了海军陆战队，去了哈佛商学院，然后毕业后，联合创办了 Cobalt Robotics，这回到了，你知道，我们通过 Bloomberg Beta 完成了种子轮融资，通过 Sequoia 完成了 A 轮，通过 CO2 完成了 B 轮。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, you know, ran that for a number of years, grew it into nine countries, four continents, having robots all over, and then sold it in 2024 and started Foundation Future Industries, which is now the sole provider of humanoids to the Department of Defense.
zh: 所以，你知道，我经营了几年，将其业务扩展到九个国家、四个大洲，到处都有我们的机器人，然后在 2024 年把它卖掉了，并创办了 Foundation Future Industries，这家公司现在是国防部人形机器人的唯一供应商。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we were talking last time we spoke about this humanoid craze that has kind of taken
zh: 所以我们要聊聊上次我们谈到的那种人形机器人热潮，这种热潮已经

speaker: Unknown
en: Over in robotics.
zh: 席卷了机器人领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was saying that it seems that there are many form factors that are more practical than the human form.
zh: 我当时说，似乎有许多比人形形态更实用的形态规格。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was asking why, and maybe you can answer for listeners, why everyone is focused on humanoids now.
zh: 我在问为什么，也许你可以为听众解答一下，为什么现在每个人都专注于人形机器人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I know that the bad answer is
zh: 我知道那个糟糕的答案是

speaker: Unknown
en: The world is built for humans.
zh: 这个世界是为人类建造的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the easiest way for robots to navigate is in the human form.
zh: 机器人导航最简单的方式就是采用人形形态。

speaker: Unknown
en: But there are all kinds of problems with the human form factors.
zh: 但是人形形态存在各种问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Balance and speed and battery life and all these different things that, frankly, it'd be easier with either
zh: 平衡性、速度、电池寿命以及所有这些不同的问题，坦率地说，用……无论是

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, I think that we're really a species of workarounds.
zh: 你知道，我认为我们实际上是一个充满变通方案的物种。

speaker: Unknown
en: In everything that we do, we have workarounds, we have shortcuts, we have ways that don't really fit the way that we're supposed to do things, but that's how they get done.
zh: 在我们所做的一切中，我们都有变通方案，都有捷径，都有一些并不真正符合我们应有做事方式的方法，但事情就是那样完成的。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's part of becoming an adult is realizing that the org chart doesn't represent the full view of relationships.
zh: 成长的一部分就是意识到组织架构图并不能代表关系的全貌。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right.
zh: 对的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so as you look at all of these workarounds, you do have all kinds of things that just need to be, you know, through a factory that need to be carried somewhere that you didn't think that they did.
zh: 所以当你审视所有这些变通方案时，确实有各种各样的事情需要，你知道，通过工厂需要被搬运到某个地方，而你没想到它们是这样做的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Things, parts that need to be discarded, things that, you know, they need to adapt.
zh: 东西、需要丢弃的零件、那些，你知道，它们需要适应的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as you really start looking at that, you need dexterity and locomotion to do it.
zh: 当你真正开始审视这一点时，你需要灵巧性和运动能力来做到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there are a lot of things you can think about what form factors that could fit.
zh: 所以你可以考虑很多适合的形态规格。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the only form factor that we know fits all of these jobs is the human form factor because humans are doing it today.
zh: 但我们知道唯一适合所有这些工作的形态规格就是人形形态，因为人类今天正在做这些工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, you know, to everyone who wonders about the human form factor, and I always did, you know, I would turn them to the question of why do we still have so many humans in all of these factories, right?
zh: 所以，对于所有怀疑人形形态的人来说，我也一直怀疑，你知道，我会把问题转向为什么我们所有这些工厂里仍有这么多人类，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: I walk into them and they're packed with robots, right?
zh: 我走进去，里面满是机器人，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: There are all kinds of ABB and FANUC and industrial robots, but there are also human beings everywhere.
zh: 有各种 ABB 和 FANUC 以及工业机器人，但也到处都是人类。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that's always my first question when I walk in, as I say, what are all these people doing here?
zh: 所以当我走进去时，这总是我的第一个问题，正如我所说，所有这些人都在这里做什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's what we'll spend the next couple hours as we tour any facility talking about is why are they still humans?
zh: 这也是我们在接下来几个小时里参观任何设施时要讨论的，就是为什么它们仍然是人类？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And is it the form, the human form, or is it the human judgment?
zh: 是形态，人形形态，还是人类的判断力？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, is it the physicality or the mental capability that humans provide?
zh: 我是说，是身体上的还是心理上的能力是人类提供的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, the human hand is incredible.
zh: 嗯，人手是不可思议的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's a big portion of it.
zh: 这是很大的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think about that every time I'm balancing a mug of coffee as I carry in groceries and have a kid in my arm.
zh: 每次我拿着一杯咖啡保持平衡，同时提着杂货手臂上还抱着个孩子时，我都会想到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm still able to open the door.
zh: 而且我仍然能够打开门。

speaker: Unknown
en: The human form factor is pretty amazing for things like that.
zh: 人形形态对于这类事情来说相当神奇。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it also is.
zh: 但它也是。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's being bipedal and being able to move around all these spaces, being able to sidestep, move forward and backwards without taking up a lot of room that wheels might or that a base might.
zh: 它是双足行走，能够在这个空间里四处移动，能够侧身移动、前后移动而不像轮子或底座那样占用太多空间。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then also the human judgment.
zh: 然后还有人类的判断力。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you put all of those things together, you start to really get an appreciation of the human design.
zh: 当你把所有这些结合起来时，你会开始真正欣赏人类的设计。

speaker: Unknown
en: You start to learn a lot about the eyes when you're going into perception.
zh: 当你进入感知领域时，你会开始了解很多关于眼睛的知识。

speaker: Unknown
en: You start looking a lot at the mouth when you have the robot have speakers.
zh: 当你给机器人配备扬声器时，你会开始大量关注嘴巴。

speaker: Unknown
en: All of these things are actually designed very well.
zh: 所有这些事物实际上都设计得非常好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, and I mean, you mentioned the hand.
zh: 是的，我是说，你提到了手。

speaker: Unknown
en: I wasn't going to go into the weeds right away, but I did a piece for somebody on the Wuji hand, this hand out of China that uses, it has the actuator.
zh: 我本不打算立刻钻进细节里，但我确实为某人写了一篇关于 Wuji hand 的文章，这是中国出产的一只手，它使用了，它有执行器。

speaker: Unknown
en: The motor, you know, instead of the most of the hands human, the robot hands today, the form human form factor hands use a tendon system.
zh: 马达，你知道，代替大多数的人手，今天的机器人手，人形形态的手使用的是肌腱系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the motors are buried in the what is the wrist and then their tendons that run up and work the fingers.
zh: 所以马达被埋在手腕里，然后有肌腱向上延伸控制手指。

speaker: Unknown
en: But there are a lot of reasons why that's not ideal.
zh: 但是有很多原因说明这不理想。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's a company in China that makes tiny actuators and they have a subsidiary.
zh: 中国有一家公司制造微型致动器，他们有一家子公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you for joining us.
zh: 感谢你们加入我们。

speaker: Unknown
en: For locomotion, but how are you guys working on dexterity?
zh: 关于运动，但你们如何处理灵巧性？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, what hands do you use?
zh: 我是说，你们使用什么样的手？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, there are two questions about the hands, I think.
zh: 嗯，关于手有两个问题，我想。

speaker: Unknown
en: One is how dexterous are they?
zh: 一个是它们有多灵巧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So how small of an object, how thin of an object can they pick up?
zh: 所以多小的物体，多薄的物体它们能捡起来？

speaker: Unknown
en: Can they pick up a pin?
zh: 它们能捡起一根针吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Can they do electrical wires, things like that?
zh: 它们能处理电线之类的东西吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: The other is in strength.
zh: 另一个是强度。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so how much can they lift?
zh: 以及它们能举多重？

speaker: Unknown
en: For how long can they lift it?
zh: 它们能举多久？

speaker: Unknown
en: Can they pull these things up?
zh: 它们能把这些东西拉起来吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: How much torque can they produce?
zh: 它们能产生多大的扭矩？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so when you're really looking at dexterity and strength, I think that there are ways to have actuators in the hand that have lots of dexterity.
zh: 所以当你真正审视灵巧性和强度时，我认为有办法在手部安置致动器以获得很高的灵巧性。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think if that's the hand that I'm thinking of, it's an incredible one.
zh: 我想如果那就是我所想的那只手，那是一只不可思议的手。

speaker: Unknown
en: Watched it all over YouTube and immediately went to my hand team and I said, why aren't we using this?
zh: 在 YouTube 上看遍了它，立刻去找我的手部团队说，为什么我们不用这个？

speaker: Unknown
en: And they wrote back, strength.
zh: 他们回复说，强度。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, as a matter of fact, that's right.
zh: 是的，事实上，没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's only got like 40% of the strength of a human hand, yeah.
zh: 它只有人类手部大约 40% 的强度，是的。

zh: 我们将达到这一点，你知道，我们的机器人可以更换彼此的电池。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, you know, you will find this fully autonomous command center.
zh: 所以，你知道，你会发现这个完全自主的指挥中心。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, that's how, I mean, this all sounds very futuristic, sounds possible, but it still sounds like it's not, we're not there today.
zh: 是的，这就是，我的意思是，这一切听起来非常未来，听起来是可能的，但它仍然听起来好像不是，我们今天还没有到那一步。

speaker: Unknown
en: How confident are you that you'll be able to deploy successfully on a battlefield in a certain time frame and what time frame are you looking at?
zh: 你对自己能够在特定时间框架内成功部署到战场上有多大信心，而你正在看的时间框架是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, I think I'm just as confident as I am that my kids are going to be able to drive cars, that they're going to get married and buy houses.
zh: 你知道，我认为我的信心就像我相信我的孩子们能够开车一样，他们会结婚并买房子。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, a lot of this is you look at it in its infancy and it is hard.
zh: 并且，你知道，这其中很多是你看着它处于萌芽阶段，它是很难的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's hard.
zh: 很难。

speaker: Unknown
en: My kids are six, seven and eight years old.
zh: 我的孩子六岁、七岁和八岁。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's hard to look at them and start thinking, oh, they're going to do taxes, right?
zh: 很难看着他们并开始思考，噢，他们要做纳税申报，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because they're not there today.
zh: 因为他们今天还没到那一步。

speaker: Unknown
en: But when you really look at how quickly they're growing and when you really think, you know, when I think back to two years ago, how my kids were talking, how they were acting, how they thought, right, and where they are today, that's where you start to go, yeah, we have this very linear view of what growth and improvement looks like.
zh: 但当你真正看他们长得有多快，当你真正思考，你知道，当我回想两年前，我的孩子们怎么说话，怎么行动，怎么思考，对吧，以及他们今天在哪里，那就是你开始说，是的，我们对成长和进步的看法是非常线性的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But for robotics especially, I think if you look 20 months ago, we didn't have a robot.
zh: 但对于机器人技术尤其如此，我认为如果你看 20 个月前，我们还没有机器人。

speaker: Unknown
en: We had smiles on our faces and the idea of humanoids, right?
zh: 我们脸上带着微笑和人形机器人的想法，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And today, we have robots already deployed out in the world working full shifts.
zh: 而今天，我们已经有了部署在世界各地的机器人，在轮班工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have robots that are ready to walk uneven surfaces and go out into the battlefield.
zh: 我们有准备好在不平坦表面行走的机器人，并走上战场。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, you know, that's all just in 20 months.
zh: 所以，你知道，这所有一切都只是在 20 个月内。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think 20 months from now is going to be shocking to a lot of people.
zh: 所以我认为从现在起 20 个月将会让很多人感到震惊。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think all of this is a lot closer than anyone will think.
zh: 我认为所有这些都比任何人想象的要近得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's talk about the Georgia deployment.
zh: 让我们谈谈佐治亚州的部署。

speaker: Unknown
en: What exactly are the robots doing?
zh: 机器人到底在做什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's almost all injection molded parts.
zh: 所以它几乎全是注塑成型部件。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, you know, all of these other FANUC robots and things all make all of these parts.
zh: 所以，你知道，所有这些其他的 FANUC 机器人和东西都在制造所有这些部件。

speaker: Unknown
en: They clip them together.
zh: 它们把它们夹在一起。

speaker: Unknown
en: They come out on a conveyor belt.
zh: 它们从传送带上出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when we arrived there, it would be, you know, a human that's standing there, a person on an eight hour shift.
zh: 当我们到达那里时，那是，你知道，一个站在那里的人，一个八小时轮班的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: The parts come out in different spaces on the conveyor belt, right?
zh: 部件在传送带的不同空间出来，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's a little bit of adaptability that needs to go on there.
zh: 所以那里需要有一点适应性。

speaker: Unknown
en: They would put a label on it.
zh: 它们会在上面贴标签。

speaker: Unknown
en: They would do a quality control check with a camera.
zh: 它们会用相机做质量检查。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then after they marked it good, they would put it into the packaging.
zh: 然后在他们标记合格后，他们会把它放入包装中。

speaker: Unknown
en: If it was bad, they would move it to a separate rack where it would get taken away.
zh: 如果是坏的，他们会把它移到一个单独的架子上，在那里它会被带走。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, you know, as we looked at that, we thought, we could probably handle something like this.
zh: 所以，你知道，当我们看着那个时，我们想，我们大概可以处理这样的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think it was, what, April to November, never do math in public, but I don't know, six months in or so, that we did a proof of concept on this.
zh: 我认为那是，什么，四月到十一月，永远不要在公开场合做数学，但我不知道，大概六个月左右，我们对此做了一个概念验证。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we brought our first robot out.
zh: 我们带出了我们的第一个机器人。

speaker: Unknown
en: That robot was on wheels.
zh: 那个机器人是轮式的。

speaker: Unknown
en: When we did it, we didn't have the legs yet.
zh: 当我们做的时候，我们还没有腿。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the robot was able to do all the parts.
zh: 机器人能够做所有部件。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we did that for hundreds of parts for all their executive team.
zh: 所以我们为他们所有的高管团队做了几百个部件。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they all said, this looks like it's worth moving forward.
zh: 他们都说，这看起来值得继续推进。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so now we have a contract for 150 robots going and doing those tasks.
zh: 所以现在我们有一个 150 个机器人去执行那些任务的合同。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's what we're deploying.
zh: 这就是我们正在部署的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we're working to get all of those robots out.
zh: 我们正在努力把所有那些机器人都弄出去。

speaker: Unknown
en: But they're very, very similar tasks.
zh: 但它们是非常、非常相似的任务。

speaker: Unknown
en: Different parts, but very similar.
zh: 不同的部件，但非常相似。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, what kind of a factory, I mean, what's the product that they're assembling?
zh: 是的，什么样的工厂，我的意思是，他们正在组装的产品是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's an automotive OEM, so it's, they make parts for, you know, they actually, they make a part for my Land Rover, you know, so it's funny as you go out there, it's a little plastic cladding part on the outside of the door, and I go, ah, you know, you can pop it off and see that's made in Georgia.
zh: 是一家汽车原始设备制造商，所以它，他们为……制造零件，你知道，他们实际上，他们为我的路虎制造了一个零件，你知道，所以当你去那里时这很有趣，那是门外面的一小块塑料覆层部件，我会说，啊，你知道，你可以把它扣下来，看看那是佐治亚州制造的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the power, presumably, was that difficult to design the cabling so that these robots don't get tangled up?
zh: 还有电源，想必，很难设计布线以免这些机器人纠缠在一起吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Not at all, oddly enough.
zh: 一点也不，奇怪的是。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, I thought that was going to be a real thing.
zh: 你知道，我以为这会是个大问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was the thing that we talked about a lot before we went out there.
zh: 这是我们去那里之前讨论得很多的一件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: But really, so all 150 of these operate in a 15 by 15 cell or smaller, 15 foot by 15 foot.
zh: 但实际上，这全部 150 个都在一个 15 乘 15 的单元或更小的空间里运行，15 英尺乘 15 英尺。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's nobody that moves that much.
zh: 没有人会移动那么多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the first robots that we've deployed, they really only take a couple steps.
zh: 我们部署的第一批机器人，它们实际上只走几步。

speaker: Unknown
en: At most, they're probably taking five steps.
zh: 最多，它们可能走五步。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it's interesting.
zh: 所以这很有趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: We'll have the robot just move backward instead of turning around and doing these things.
zh: 我们会让机器人直接向后移动，而不是转身去做这些事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the cable really just hangs there.
zh: 所以电缆真的就挂在那里。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like my dog when I put him on a running leash out there.
zh: 就像我把它放在跑步牵引绳上时的狗一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: It just doesn't get tangled.
zh: 它就是不会缠在一起。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, that's interesting, the dog analogy.
zh: 是的，这很有趣，那个狗的比喻。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you guys are 20 months in.
zh: 所以你们已经进行了 20 个月。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, it's incredible.
zh: 我的意思是，这令人难以置信。

speaker: Unknown
en: And maybe it's the fearlessness that comes with someone coming in fresh.
zh: 也许这是一种初来乍到者带来的无畏。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know, because a lot of the researchers that I've talked to are so...
zh: 我不知道，因为我交谈过的许多研究人员都非常……

speaker: Unknown
en: ...cautious about capabilities.
zh: ……对能力持谨慎态度。

speaker: Unknown
en: And frankly, what I've seen until fairly recently with Optimus, they don't blow me away and they don't look very robust.
zh: 坦白说，直到最近我在 Optimus 上看到的，它们并没有让我感到震撼，看起来也不太稳健。

speaker: Unknown
en: But you guys have made all this progress in 20 months.
zh: 但你们在 20 个月内取得了所有这些进展。

speaker: Unknown
en: Where do you see this going for you and for the industry?
zh: 你认为这对你们和该行业未来将走向何方？

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, to me, this really is one of those cases where the attitude and approach makes a huge difference in how the technology develops.
zh: 你知道，对我来说，这确实是态度和方法对技术发展方式产生巨大影响的案例之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, I think everybody saw there was a viral video.
zh: 你知道，我想每个人都看到过那个病毒式传播的视频。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it was out of Germany or Russia.
zh: 我想那是来自德国或俄罗斯。

speaker: Unknown
en: I can't remember where it was out of, but the robot that walked on stage and fell and
zh: 我不记得它是哪里的，但是那个走上舞台然后摔倒的机器人，而且

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, and the guys run out to cover it like a car accident and they're very frantic about it.
zh: 是的，那些人跑出来像掩盖车祸一样把它盖住，他们对此非常慌乱。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is not hard to find videos of our robot falling.
zh: 找到我们的机器人摔倒的视频并不难。

speaker: Unknown
en: But what you'll see when it falls, you know, is Sanket and I will be standing next to it.
zh: 但你会看到当它摔倒时，你知道，Sanket 和我会站在它旁边。

speaker: Unknown
en: It will fall and we continue conducting the interview as we lift it back up and get the robot working.
zh: 它会摔倒，我们在把它扶起来并让机器人重新工作的同时继续进行采访。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because I...
zh: 因为我……

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that we, coming into this, we're not shy about saying this is very new technology.
zh: 我认为我们，进入这个领域时，并不讳言这是非常新的技术。

speaker: Unknown
en: All of the stuff that we're solving, we're very honest about where it's at.
zh: 我们正在解决的所有问题，我们都非常诚实地对待它的现状。

speaker: Unknown
en: But as you do that throughout the whole team and you don't have these kind of marketing lies that are built up and things that you're hiding behind and trying to make these highly curated videos, you have a team that is actually able to deal with the problem that's happening.
zh: 但当你让整个团队都这样做，并且没有这些建立起来的营销谎言，也没有你在背后隐藏的东西，试图制作这些精心策划的视频时，你就有了一个能够实际解决正在发生的问题的团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when you have very smart people that are directed toward those problems, you can get those problems solved.
zh: 当你有非常聪明的人被指派去解决那些问题时，你就能解决这些问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I do think this is an interesting time where the experts in all the specific tasks have kind of too much project fatigue for them to really see how quickly this is going to move.
zh: 所以我确实认为这是一个有趣的时间，所有特定任务上的专家都有太多的项目疲劳，以至于无法真正看到这会发展得有多快。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I'm still shocked.
zh: 所以我仍然感到震惊。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll talk to other founders and they'll be saying, you know, yeah, I think we're 10 to 15 years out.
zh: 我会和其他创始人交谈，他们会说，是的，我认为我们还有 10 到 15 年的路要走。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I go, you better get ready because we're making 10,000 this year and I'm not going to keep those in a storage unit.
zh: 我会说，你最好做好准备，因为我们今年要制造 10,000 个，我不会把它们放在储藏室里。

speaker: Unknown
en: These things are getting out in the world.
zh: 这些东西正进入世界。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, and that's, I think I told you, I wrote something last year, early last year, about a year ago, about humanoids and how the promise is way out ahead of the reality.
zh: 是的，这，我想告诉过你，我去年写了一些东西，去年年初，大约一年前，关于人形机器人，以及它的承诺是如何远远领先于现实的。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are all these problems with power supply and the strength of actuators and the generalization of the models that control them.
zh: 电源供应、致动器的强度以及控制它们的模型的泛化能力都存在所有这些问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Particularly, there was talk, and there continues to be, of household robots that will be your housekeeper.
zh: 特别是，有关于，并且持续有关于将成为你的管家的家用机器人的讨论。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I have been very...
zh: 而我一直非常……

speaker: Unknown
en: not skeptical that it won't happen someday but that we're even within 10 or 15 years of that that it's going to take a long time to get that level
zh: 并不是怀疑它有一天不会发生，而是怀疑我们是否能在 10 年或 15 年内达到那个水平，达到那个水平需要很长时间

speaker: Unknown
en: This is so funny because I have, you know, from your alma mater, well, I call it the New York Times, I have hanging on my wall, the New York Times, you can print any old copy of the newspaper, any page, right?
zh: 这太搞笑了，因为，你知道，从你的母校，嗯，我称之为《纽约时报》，我的墙上挂着《纽约时报》，你可以打印任何旧版的报纸，任何一页，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I went through the archives and found in, I think it's 1906, I think it's October 1906, there is an article that says why there will never be heavier than air flight.
zh: 所以我翻阅了档案，在，我想是 1906 年，我想是 1906 年 10 月，有一篇文章说为什么永远不会有重于空气的飞行

speaker: Unknown
en: And it says, so many people have been trying planes.
zh: 它说，有太多人都在尝试飞机

speaker: Unknown
en: And the analogy that it uses, this is the math that it does.
zh: 它使用的类比是，这是它所做的数学计算

speaker: Unknown
en: It says, if you look at how long it took birds to evolve,
zh: 它说，如果你看看鸟类进化花了多长时间，

speaker: Unknown
en: Right?
zh: 对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: You would already have almost a million years.
zh: 你差不多会有一百万年

speaker: Unknown
en: And to do that with metal, which is even heavier, is going to be even harder.
zh: 而且用金属来做这件事，金属甚至更重，将会更加困难

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the writer says that it's going to be between 1 million and 10 million years for human beings to achieve flight.
zh: 所以作者说，人类实现飞行需要在一百万到一千万年之间

speaker: Unknown
en: And three months later, you had the Wright brothers that were first in flight.
zh: 而三个月后，莱特兄弟就首次飞行了

speaker: Unknown
en: So I have that framed on my wall because I think that we are living in exactly that time where the humanoids are in their infancy.
zh: 所以我把那个装裱在墙上，因为我认为我们正生活在那个时代，人形机器人正处于婴儿期

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that a lot of people working on them don't believe in them.
zh: 我认为许多从事这方面工作的人并不相信它们

speaker: Unknown
en: I think a lot of them still think, yeah, there's funding coming in, but these things aren't going to turn out.
zh: 我认为他们很多人仍然认为，是的，有资金进来，但这东西不会成功

speaker: Unknown
en: But as I look at this, we are the Wright brothers.
zh: 但当我看着这个时，我们是莱特兄弟

speaker: Unknown
en: These are going to be working far sooner than anybody thinks, and people are going to be shocked at the change that it makes in the world.
zh: 这些东西投入使用的时间将比任何人认为的要早得多，人们将会震惊于它给世界带来的变化

speaker: Unknown
en: Hyundai is famously, as they were featured on 60 Minutes, using or at least talking about deploying Boston Atlas, Boston Dynamics humanoid.
zh: 现代汽车众所周知，正如他们在《60 分钟》节目中亮相的那样，正在使用或至少谈论部署 Boston Atlas，Boston Dynamics 的人形机器人

speaker: Unknown
en: When Boston Dynamics is tied up with DeepMind, Google DeepMind, who
zh: 当 Boston Dynamics 与 DeepMind、Google DeepMind 挂钩时，他们

speaker: Unknown
en: It would be terrifying to me to have to compete with them.
zh: 对我来说，必须与他们竞争将是可怕的

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, first of all, with Boston Dynamics, because they've been at this for such a long time, and the criticism of their robots used to be, yeah, but it's all teleoperated.
zh: 我的意思是，首先，对于 Boston Dynamics，因为他们从事这方面已经很长时间了，而且对他们的机器人的批评过去是，是的，但这都是远程遥控的

speaker: Unknown
en: There's no AI controlling the robot.
zh: 没有 AI 控制机器人

speaker: Unknown
en: But now they've got DeepMind, and they've got a...
zh: 但现在他们有了 DeepMind，他们有了一个...

speaker: Unknown
en: A refined form factor.
zh: 精炼的外形规格

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, it's pretty impressive.
zh: 我的意思是，这非常令人印象深刻

speaker: Unknown
en: In the video, I saw doing something similar to what you're talking about in Georgia of picking up parts, scanning it for defects, and then moving it to where it needs to be.
zh: 在视频中，我看到他们在做类似你所说的在乔治亚州的事情，拿起零件，扫描缺陷，然后把它移动到需要的地方

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you see the competitive landscape?
zh: 你如何看待竞争格局？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is this a market that is going to be so large that
zh: 这是一个将非常巨大的市场，以至于

speaker: Unknown
en: There will be many players, or do you feel pressure from people like Boston Dynamics and DeepBrain?
zh: 会有许多参与者，还是你感受到来自 Boston Dynamics 和 DeepBrain 等人的压力？

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, we feel a lot of pressure.
zh: 哦，我们感受到很大的压力

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, absolutely.
zh: 是的，绝对如此

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, this is, and that's why we work, you know, six days, some of our teams work six days a week, some teams work seven days a week.
zh: 我的意思是，这是一场，这就是为什么我们要工作，你知道，六天，我们的一些团队每周工作六天，一些团队每周工作七天

speaker: Unknown
en: Because this is a huge race against all of these.
zh: 因为这是一场与所有这些进行的巨大竞赛

speaker: Unknown
en: But when I look at Boston Dynamics, I loved watching that 60 minutes.
zh: 但当我看着 Boston Dynamics 时，我喜欢看那个《60 分钟》

speaker: Unknown
en: I watched it with my kids getting ready the other day, the other morning.
zh: 有一天早上，我前一天和孩子们一起做准备时看的

speaker: Unknown
en: They are doing almost exactly the same task.
zh: 他们做的几乎完全相同的任务

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you look at what the parts they're using, I mean, they look almost identical to what they're doing.
zh: 所以如果你看他们使用的零件，我的意思是，它们看起来和他们在做的几乎一模一样
